verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The phone rings twice in an empty house and then stops.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles back on the receiver's cradle—
someone, somewhere, changed their mind about needing us.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Outside, a car idles at the curb, then pulls away—
whatever they came to say
folded back into its envelope of silence.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The envelope sits unopened on the table—
we learn to read the shapes of things
by the silence they leave behind them.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Morning light moves across the table's grain,
finds the envelope, moves on—
even the sun won't ask what's written there.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dust from verse one settles here too,
a fine grey script across the sealed flap—
some questions get answered just by waiting long enough.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone finally lifts it, weighs it in their palm—
whatever answer dust had written
scatters at the touch, and starts again.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The paper's edge cuts a thin line on the thumb—
proof that opening costs something,
before a single word gets read.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A drop of blood, small as a period,
lands on the unopened fold—
already writing its own ending.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The fold accepts it like an old debt—
red sinking into fiber, into grain,
before the reading even starts to hurt.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Now the crease keeps a secret color—
whoever unfolds it next will read
a sentence written before the words arrived.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mail truck idles at the curb regardless—
it doesn't know what it's delivering,
only that the schedule says: today.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A hand will reach into the box tonight,
expecting bills, a postcard, nothing much—
not this small weight that already knows its name.
motifs: a hand reaching into a box
an object that knows its name

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Whatever it is, it will sit on the table first,
next to the salt and the unpaid gas bill,
pretending to be something that can wait.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone will pass it twice before touching it,
the way you circle a sleeping dog—
not sure if it's the waking or the silence you're afraid of.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
By the third pass they'll touch it like a pulse,
two fingers testing what the quiet means—
not asleep, then. Just waiting to be sure of them.
